_meta.description: Authoritative New York regional taxonomy for the Carevero NY foundation. Consumer-facing regions derived from New York State's 10 Regional Economic Development Council (REDC) regions, adapted for a healthcare consumer: New York City is split into its five boroughs (first-class regions) that roll up to 'New York City' via region_groups, because a single giant NYC bucket would bury hospital discovery. Long Island (Nassau+Suffolk) stays one region. All other regions map 1:1 to REDC. Every one of NY's 62 counties resolves to exactly one region purely from the CMS county (countyparish); no municipality subdivision is required (unlike MA). IDENTITY/geography only — no pricing, nothing consumer-published. Validated against data/ny_cms_hospital_snapshot.json (dataset xubh-q36u, retrieved 2026-08-23) via scripts/verify_ny_foundation.py: every denominator hospital resolves to its assigned region from county.

region_groups._note: Consumer roll-up areas. NYC's five boroughs roll up to 'New York City' so a query like 'MRI in NYC' spans all five; every other region is its own group. Every region appears in exactly one group (verified).

municipal_overrides._note: NY regions are cleanly county-based, so no city-level exceptions are currently needed. Reserved for future cross-boundary edge cases (checked before county rules).
